method: News coverage and campaign-trail reporting scored for narrative direction (favorite gaining/losing ground) and intensity (fundraising, endorsements, gaffes, message discipline). This is NOT a poll - it's a bounded nudge applied only to toss-up/lean seats, capped at +/-0.08 win probability, and always shown separately from the polling-based number.

assessments.rationale: Recent polling shows Talarico (D) with a slight edge over Paxton (R) in a dead-heat race. Multiple polls from late August/early September show Talarico leading by 0.6-3 points (UT/TPP, Overton Insights, Emerson tied at 47-46). Cook moved race to Toss Up. Race remains very close but slight Democratic momentum evident.

Michigan Senate race is a dead heat between El-Sayed (D) and Rogers (R). Recent polls show mixed results - some with El-Sayed up 1-5 points, others with Rogers narrowly ahead. Decision Desk HQ average shows El-Sayed +2. Latest Detroit News poll shows Rogers with razor-thin lead. Race remains toss-up with slight Republican momentum from recent polling.

Former Sen. Brown (D) showing surprising strength against appointed Sen. Husted (R) in Republican-leaning Ohio. Decision Desk HQ average shows Brown leading 49%-44%. Fox News poll shows Brown ahead by 8 points. 33% of respondents say Husted is too close to Trump. Brown's history of outperforming Democratic baseline in Ohio showing in polls.

Former Gov. Cooper (D) showing strong lead over Whatley (R) in North Carolina. RCP average shows Cooper +8.0. Recent polls show Cooper leading by 7-11 points (Elon 53-42, Carolina Forward 50-43, High Point 50-45). Cooper holds 28-point advantage among independents. Democrats' best pickup opportunity per Decision Desk HQ forecast.

Sen. Ossoff (D) showing strong lead over Collins (R) in Georgia. Pollsmax average shows Ossoff +7.5 (50.1-42.6). Fox News poll from late June showed Ossoff leading by 13 points (56-43). Ossoff has strong support from independents (68% in Fox poll) and is outperforming expectations in Trump-won state. Collins faces challenges with ethics investigation and controversial positions.

Sen. Collins (R) defending seat against Jackson (D) in Maine with ranked-choice voting. Collins is only GOP senator from state Trump never won, making it competitive. Jackson replaced primary winner Platner who withdrew in July. Limited recent polling available. Race rated toss-up by Cook, but Collins' incumbency and moderate profile balanced against national environment.

Sen. Sullivan (R) facing former Rep. Peltola (D) in Alaska with ranked-choice voting. Peltola narrowly lost House seat in 2024 but showed ability to win statewide. Sullivan incumbent advantage balanced against Peltola's name recognition and ranked-choice system that helped her win in 2022 House special. Limited recent polling. Neutral adjustment in absence of clear momentum signals.

Rep. Hinson (R) vs. state Rep. Turek (D) for open seat in Iowa. Cook moved race to Toss Up on Aug 20. Hinson won GOP primary with 73.9% backed by Trump. Iowa hasn't elected Democrat to Senate since 2008. Limited recent polling, but Republicans have structural advantage in state trending red. Slight Republican lean in absence of strong Democratic polling.

Rep. Pappas (D) vs. former Sen. John E. Sununu (R) for open seat. Recent UNH poll (Aug 26) shows Sununu leading 45-43%, a shift from June when Pappas led 47-44%. Emerson poll shows statistical tie. Race surprisingly competitive - NH hasn't had close Senate race since 2016. Republicans bullish but Cook notes difficult to see GOP upset in favorable Democratic environment. Slight Republican momentum evident from recent polling trend.

Sen. Roger Marshall (R) seeking reelection in Kansas against Democratic nominee. Cook rates race Lean R. Marshall recently in news criticizing Trump's call to ban Bombardier planes, showing some independence. Kansas is Republican-leaning state; Democrats unlikely to flip without exceptional candidate or conditions. Limited polling available. Slight Republican advantage expected given state fundamentals.
